subject.title: The Skill Accumulation Problem: How many skills before your agent gets confused?

question: Should ClawHub own task-context skill recommendations and skill-to-skill conflict metadata, or should this issue be narrowed to registry guidance while OpenClaw owns runtime loading policy?
rationale: Current main covers global ranking, category-related browsing, executable dependency declarations, and local pinning, but the remaining behavior changes public metadata, recommendation privacy inputs, and potentially another repository's runtime semantics.

options.title: Specify a split contract
options.body: Define ClawHub metadata and recommendation boundaries separately from OpenClaw runtime loading and tool-collision policy before implementation.

options.title: Limit this to guidance
options.body: Keep product contracts unchanged and document pruning, layering, dependency declarations, and pinning practices.

options.title: Build ClawHub governance
options.body: Design first-class task-context recommendations and conflict metadata in ClawHub with explicit privacy and compatibility rules.

recommendation.title: Specify a split contract
recommendation.body: Define ClawHub metadata and recommendation boundaries separately from OpenClaw runtime loading and tool-collision policy before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant schema, API, CLI, recommendation, and ownership history points most strongly to this owner.
